To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have analytically calculated the next-to-leading-order QCD correction to the energy-energy correlation in the gluon initiated H+H− decay process, expressed in terms of the classical polylogarithm functions.
we have analytically computed the EEC function for gluon-initiated gluon fusion decays of the Higgs boson to NLO accuracy in the HEFT framework.
we calculated the EEC observable in gluon-initated Higgs decay at NLO analytically, in terms of classical multiple polylogarithms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the strong interactions between elementary particles, and in particular with the determination of the parameters of the standard model of particle physics, which is currently the most successful theory in physics.
the analytic calculation of energy-energy correlator in gluon-initated Higgs decay at NLO accuracy in the HEFT framework, and the study of the phenomenological implications of this observable.
the study of the energy-energy correlation ( EEC ) function in the Higgs decay in the framework of Higgs Effective Field Theories ( HEFT ).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the energy-energy correlation function in gluon-initated Higgs decay is calculated analytically at the next-to leading order in Higgs Effective Field Theories, and the results are expressed in terms of the polylogarithm functions, including the asymptotics in the collinear limit.
the analytic results for the EEC function at the NLO are now available for all the main processes of interest for the e+e− Higgs factories.
this work is a first step towards a complete analytic calculation of energy-energy correlations for gluon initiated processes in the HEFT.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we provide the full analytic NLO results for the EEC observable in gluon initiated Higg decays and provide a detailed discussion on the numerical aspects of our calculation.

, for the first time, we have analytically computed an NLO QCD observable in gluon initiated H → gg decays in the HEFT framework, which is an important step towards the full NLO QCD calculation in gluon initiated gluon fusion Higgs decays.
we have completed the analytic calculation of the EEC observable at NLO in HEFT.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NLO EEC observable in the HEFT framework is a very complicated function with many logarithmic and non-logarithmic terms.

we have shown how the EEC observable can be calculated analytically at the NLO level in a model-independent way in the HEFT framework, which is a powerful tool to probe the Higgs sector at future lepton colliders.
the NLO corrections to the EEC observable in Higgs decay is significantly smaller than those in e+e- collisions.
